industries.narrative: SPAC/shell tape driven by heavy relative volume (3.3x) and cap-weighted move despite weak breadth — event-driven, name-specific action rather than broad theme.

sector_breadth_notes.note: XLF strength is extraordinarily narrow — only Shell Companies clears the gate while Insurance-Specialty is a bottom-10 laggard. Not a broad financials move.
XLK is hollow at the industry level: Semis, Semi Equipment, Computer Hardware and Electronic Components all rank in the bottom 5 — sector ETF strength is masking severe internal weakness.
XLI qualifying at sector level is misleading — Security Services, Farm Machinery, and Pollution Controls are all deeply weak with near-zero advancers.
XLY breadth is thin — Personal Services and Lodging show 0% advancing, suggesting consumer discretionary strength is concentrated in a few mega-caps.

key_divergences: Massive divergence: six sectors qualified at the ETF level but only one narrow industry (Shell Companies) qualifies underneath. XLK especially rotten — semis and hardware among the weakest industries despite XLK screening strong. Sector-level signals are being driven by mega-cap concentration, not breadth.
leadership_theme: Event-driven SPAC/shell tape only; broad industry participation absent across all six qualifying sectors.
